resources.string: The answer helps to know which games work, and is sent to the project without any name.
The answer stays on this device: sending is off in Settings.

Only the game, the answer, the version of GamePort and the kind of device are sent. After \"It did not work\" or \"Works offline only\", a technical report is sent too. The choice is in Settings > Account.
Sorry it did not work. A small technical report goes with the answer: versions, files and logs of the game, never a name, an e-mail address or an account.
Thanks for the answer. A small technical report goes with it: versions, files and logs of the game, never a name, an e-mail address or an account.
The report will be sent as soon as this device is online.
Automatic sending is off in Settings, so the report was not sent.
The report could not be sent.
No report could be made for this game.
The report could not be saved.
A few words help a lot: the report shows how the game ran, not what was seen.

resources.string: Not patched now because they are on screen: %1$s.
Some games are patched without any confirmation and others ask for one: it is a constraint of the game, not of GamePort.
Some games were not patched and can be patched from their page: %1$s.
Games made for VR and ordinary games are kept apart. The tabs switch between them, and the shoulder buttons of a controller do the same.
Games that just got an Android version. A game owned on Steam opens its page, any other opens its page in the store.
Every game of the Steam account that can be used here. A cover opens the page of the game, and a long press opens a menu with the quick actions.
Finds a game by its name in the library.
Narrows the library, for example to installed games only. The number on the button says how many filters are on, so a filter left on is never a mystery.

Every game of Steam that has an Android version, whether the account has it or not. Filters narrow the list, for example to the games not owned yet, and a free game can be added to the Steam account from its page.
What is being downloaded, patched and installed, with the progress of each game.
What players report for every game: works, works offline only, mixed or does not work. It helps to pick a game before installing it.
The Steam account, downloads, appearance, updates, and a Help section with every label explained and every tour.
What is known about the game
The labels say whether the game is for VR, whether it is owned or shared, and what players report: works, offline only, mixed, problems or incompatible. Settings > Help shows every case.

When an installed game needs something, a notice appears here with its action: a new version, a newer patch, a missing permission, saves that differ, controllers to remap. Nothing is shown when all is well.

The main button installs the game, then starts it. While it downloads, a card shows the steps and the extra content, and it can be paused or cancelled. When a new version or a newer patch is waiting, the button asks what to do first.

What wants a look: a new version, a newer patch, saves that do not agree with Steam, a game adapted by GamePort. The bell carries their number and opens or closes the card; each line leads to what it is about.
Everything else about the game in one panel: its saves, its Workshop, its controllers, its compatibility options, reporting a problem, its page in the shop, favorites, hiding it, and uninstalling it.
Saves are kept in sync with Steam Cloud. An orange dot says the saves on this device and on Steam do not agree, and the page explains which one is newer.
Prepares a report with the logs of the game and sends it to the project, without any name or account.
The options that make a game work: use the controls of the Steam Frame, and follow the recentering of the device. A small dot says GamePort adapted the game by itself.
Maps the buttons of the controls the game expects onto the controllers of this device. The color says whether the Steam Frame controls are forced or set up automatically.
Settings kept for this game only, such as the height of the player.
The size of the download and of the installed game, and the time played on this device and on Steam.
A short tour explains the labels, notices and buttons of a game\'s page. It is offered only once, and can be started again from Settings > Help.
Shows every game with an Android version, only the VR ones or only the flat ones. It appears on devices that run VR.
Finds a game by its name among the games with an Android version.
Opens the filters of the list. The number on the button says how many are on, so a filter left on is never a mystery.
Orders the list, for example by name, rating, popularity, release date, price or discount.

Three switches on one row: what can be installed or is coming, what the Steam account has or not, and what works on this device or not. All, the first position of each, shows every game, including those nobody rated.
A game of the library opens its own page, and any other opens its page in the store, which sends to Steam. Covers show the price and a mark for what players report.
Over the picture, the labels say what kind of game it is and what players report for this kind of device.

The first button opens the game on Steam, with its price and the history of its prices. For a game already in the library, another button opens its page. A free game or demo can be added to the library from here, after a confirmation that names it.
The facts about the game and the languages Steam lists for it, as a table.
Finds a game of the table by its name.
Keeps only the games that work, or only those with problems. Touching a filter again takes it off.

Each card shows how many players answered and the numbers for the kind of device in use. The outline and the label at the bottom right give the verdict. A game of the account opens its page, any other opens its page in the store.
The arrow unfolds the numbers for the other kinds of device. It is greyed when nobody answered with another.
Every game being downloaded, patched or installed, and the ones already installed. The list is empty when nothing is going on.
With several games that have a new version, a line offers to update them all at once.
Each game has its line: the steps and progress while it installs, then buttons to pause, resume, cancel or discard, to update, play or uninstall. The name opens the page of the game.

Forces the detection of the Steam Frame\'s controllers. Useful when the game starts but does not react to the controllers. A warning appears when no control for them was seen the last time the game ran.
Automatic, On or Off. Useful when recentering does not bring the game back in front. Automatic decides by itself, and says so when it turned recentering on.
Off, GamePort\'s default mapping applies. On, the choices below apply to this game. It is available once the Steam Frame\'s controls are put on this device\'s controllers.
Each control of the Steam Frame\'s controllers is listed with where it goes on this device\'s controllers. Selecting one opens a list where one or more destinations are ticked.
Erases the choices for this game, and GamePort\'s mapping applies again.
Looks again at the saves on this device and on Steam Cloud.
Says whether the saves on this device and on Steam are the same, when each was last seen, and warns when the device is offline.
Each save file with its state on this device and on Steam.
Two ways: restore Steam\'s saves onto this device, or send this device\'s saves to Steam. The change happens the next time the game starts, after a confirmation, and a safety copy is kept first.
The first button shows the games as a low list, with several games on a row, so a lot of them are seen at once.
Pressed again while the list is shown, the button goes to another number of games a row. The number is written on it.
And again: it goes round 2, 3 and 4 games a row.
The second button shows the covers, larger, with the price and the mark of what players report on each. The tour then puts back the display chosen before.

The settings are in categories: the Steam account, downloads, appearance, the home, language, updates, the management of installed games, the default configuration of games, hidden and incompatible games, and Help.

The accent colour of buttons and highlights, and the gradient behind every page, ready-made or picked colour by colour, with the size of covers and more. The tour tries a few, then puts back the ones chosen.
Where the complete tour and the tour of each page are started again, with every label, notice and button explained, and the link to the Discord.
Games that may be missing files

These games have large files beside their app, and GamePort cannot check that they are all in place:

%1$s

If one does not start or lacks content, open its page and press Repair: its large files are downloaded again, and the game stays installed.
